title: Evaluating video: a flicker metric
hook: Two simple flicker scores, tested on clips where we know the answer. Both are fooled by a pan, and one step fixes that.

verified.claim: Our studio's flicker_score is the mean absolute second difference on 128 x 128 luma from 0 to 255, and returns 0.0 below 3 frames.
We ran that formula over the whole of each web copy with ffmpeg and PIL, giving the table in this lesson.
The recorded scores for the two virtual-set shots, 3.2 and 2.0, are in the studio's data.
nm_video validates and runs on a CPU.

unchecked: Our table runs on small compressed web copies, over whole clips. The recorded 3.2 and 2.0 ran on the original renders over a middle section. So they differ, and we cannot say by how much from each cause.
FLICKER_MAX of 6.0 is labelled a starting guess in qc.py. Nothing here calibrates it against people's judgement.
The aligned score uses a single whole-pixel sideways shift per pair, on synthetic clips. A real clip has many motions in one frame and needs real flow, which we did not run.
These scores do not predict how people rate flicker. Published perceptual metrics exist, and we did not compare against them.
The first version of this lesson cited three papers by number and title. We could not confirm them, and removed them.
